text:
Loss reduction determines whether 75% terminal-only examples means 75% objective weight. The [BERT4Rec paper, Eq. 8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690) normalizes each sequence’s loss by its number of masked targets; averaging these sequence losses gives equal weight per example. The [authors’ implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py#L327-L366), however, sums target losses across the batch and divides by the total valid-target count. This gives equal weight per supervised position, so random-mask examples with multiple targets receive more total weight. Padding targets contribute neither loss nor denominator.

Derived consequence: let p=0.75, and let m be the expected target count in the random-reconstruction branch. Expected supervision is p+(1−p)m=0.75+0.25m targets/example. With pooled target averaging, the terminal-only branch’s approximate share of loss coefficients is p/[p+(1−p)m]=3/(3+m), rather than 75%. For independent masking at rate r over n eligible nonpadding items, m=rn: r=0.15 and n=50 gives m=7.5, 2.625 targets/example, and only 28.6% terminal-only coefficient share. Higher masking rates or longer histories reduce this share. Forced masks, rounding and target caps change m; use the sampler’s actual expected count.

With per-example masked-position means followed by a batch mean, terminal-only examples retain 75% expected coefficient weight regardless of m, although supervision count still changes. Random reconstruction can additionally supervise the terminal position, so terminal-only branch weight differs from total terminal-position weight. These are coefficient allocations, not guaranteed loss-value or gradient shares. Changing branch probability alone therefore changes both objective allocation and target volume; its effect depends on the existing reduction.
